Subject: Clarifying PHI scope for call transcription & BAA eligibility

Hi Jonas,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot to transcribe patient-provider calls. We need to understand whether this flow is considered PHI under your deployments and what contractual commitments (BAA) and technical controls you offer. High-level details:

- Source: short (2-10 min) recorded audio uploaded by clinicians to our web portal.
- Processing: audio is sent to Redwood's transcription endpoint and returned as text; we then run PII redaction on our side.
- Volume: pilot ~1k calls/month.

Questions we need answered quickly for the security review:
1) Is an audio transcription service treated as PHI by Redwood if the audio includes patient identifiers?
2) Can Redwood sign a BAA for this usage, and if so, which deployment options are eligible (hosted API vs. Dedicated vs. Private)?
3) What data retention does Redwood apply to uploads, transcriptions, logs, and model caches? Is there any persistent storage of raw audio or transcription tokens?
4) Does Redwood use customer-provided data to fine-tune or retrain models?

I've attached our completed SIG-lite and a flow diagram for context (CareSelect_SIG_2027.pdf, transcription_flow_v2.png). We'd like to run a brief technical call this week.

Thanks — looking forward to a quick clarification so we can move this through our procurement.

Best,
Elizabeth Grant
Security & Risk Lead
CareSelect Health

Subject: Re: Clarifying PHI scope for call transcription & BAA eligibility

Hi Elizabeth — thanks for the materials and the clear flow diagram. Quick answers up front, then a few clarifying requests so we can provide precise evidence:

1) PHI scope: Yes — if the audio contains patient identifiers (names, MRNs, dates linked to an individual, etc.) Redwood treats the resulting transcript as PHI.

2) BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA, but BAAs are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. Our hosted multi-tenant API is not BAA-eligible by default. For a pilot, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with customer isolation) is often the pragmatic first step.

3) Retention: Default hosted behavior (non-BAA) retains short-term request logs for troubleshooting; for BAA-backed Dedicated/Private customers we offer configurable retention windows and can disable long-term logging. We do not persist raw audio to model training datasets.

4) Model training: Redwood does not use customer production data to fine-tune or train public models. We separate telemetry used for platform ops from any research datasets; any use of customer-origin data for model improvements is only with explicit consent and contractual terms.

To ensure our security team provides the exact artifacts and the right SOC/SIG pages, can you confirm these details:
- Will the audio be uploaded directly to Redwood endpoints, or will CareSelect host audio in your S3 and only send links/URL references?
- Do you require transcripts to be retained in Redwood storage beyond ephemeral processing?
- Are post-transcription PII redaction steps performed client-side (CareSelect) or server-side (Redwood) in your planned flow?

I'll loop in Hannah (our Security lead) and Marissa on the next message with evidence and a recommended pilot configuration for BAA onboarding. If you want, here's a Calendly link to pick a time: https://calendly.com/redwood/tech-call-30min

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elizabeth — Hannah here (security & compliance). Thanks for the clear follow-ups — below are concrete answers and the next steps for a BAA-backed pilot.

1) Deployment & BAA: Confirming Jonas' note — BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private. For your pilot (pre-signed S3 URLs, CareSelect-controlled audio) we recommend Dedicated: it gives a single-tenant GPU pool + network isolation while keeping onboarding time lower than a full on-prem package.

2) Storage & retention options:
- Raw audio: Redwood will not persist canonical copies of audio unless explicitly enabled. With your pre-signed URL approach, Redwood will stream/process the audio and discard local copies immediately after successful transcription (we can configure zero-second retention).
- Transcripts: Default behavior for BAA-backed Dedicated can be configured to never persist transcripts server-side (returned to caller only). If you require server-side retention for troubleshooting, we support a short, auditable retention window (configurable, typical values 0, 24, 72 hours) with strict access controls and audit logs.
- Logs & telemetry: We collect limited operational telemetry for health and billing; for BAA customers telemetry can be minimized and anonymized. App-level request/response logs are opt-in and can be disabled.

3) KV cache & tokenization:
- Our inference runtime uses an in-memory KV cache to accelerate attention for long sequences. For Dedicated deployments this cache is resident only in GPU node memory and ephemeral — it is not written to disk or object storage by default.
- We can deploy nodes with encrypted swap disabled and explicit memory scrubbing on process termination for additional assurance.

4) Model training & data use: Redwood does not use customer production content to train or fine-tune public models. Any programmatic use of customer data for model improvement is only with explicit opt-in and contractual terms; we will not include CareSelect data without signed consent.

5) Sandbox / evaluation environment: We can provide a short-lived evaluation sandbox (isolated tenant with test credentials) for you to run synthetic PHI payloads. That environment will mirror the Dedicated runtime but be clearly labeled as a test tenant; sandbox activity will not be used for model training.

Attachments provided here: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (selected SOC 2 sections relevant to access controls and encryption), BAA_Onboarding_Checklist.md (step-by-step). I can also produce a redacted SIG matrix mapping if useful.

Next steps we suggest:
- Sign an NDA/Mutual NDA (if not already in place) — we can exchange an initial BAA draft after NDA.
- Schedule a 30-minute technical call to confirm the pre-signed URL flow and retention settings (https://calendly.com/redwood/tech-call-30min).
- Share any specific SIG control IDs you'd like us to annotate for Dedicated.

If you'd like, I can join the technical call and walk through the runtime memory/cache behavior live.

—Hannah Schmitt
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
